newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on likely central bank move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on likely central bank move.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed its recent depreciation to close higher against the U.S. currency on Thursday as the central bank likely intervened to prevent the local dollar from falling further, dealers said.
"Absolutely, the big brother (the central bank) had entered," said one senior dealer. "Investors, seeing that the Taiwan dollar could not fall further, turned to sell U.S. dollars," he said.
The local unit once fell to T$27.910, but U.S. dollar sales emerged to send the Taiwan dollar up to close at its intraday high of T$27.869, against Wednesday's T$27.880 finish.
Turnover was an active US$297 million.
Wednesday's close was a 12-month low for the local currency.
Another dealer alleged the central bank's Thursday intervention, a move which the bank itself seldom admits.
"I have no doubt the central bank entered in early afternoon trade and just a few minutes before the close," she said.
Dealers said as month-end U.S. dollar demand nears its end, the Taiwan dollar likely would consolidate around the current levels for several sessions.
But they maintained earlier forecasts that the local dollar then would continue to spiral downward to test a long-time support at the T$28 level.
For Friday, a T$27.86-27.92 range was seen.
